products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室) is a non-profit, government-affiliated research institution based in Shanghai, China. The laboratory describes itself as working across areas including large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for science, and foundational platforms. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading Chinese universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's primary AI product is InternLM, a Chinese open-source large language model intended for academic research. It has also released what it calls the Intern-Robotics full-stack embodied intelligence engine, described as addressing the end-to-end chain from data and training through to real-world application in robotics. At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference science forum, the laboratory announced a scientific discovery platform called Shu Sheng Duan Yan (书生·端砚), which connects science-oriented large models, specialist agents, experimental data, and physical automation equipment to support the full research workflow from hypothesis to experimental validation. Ten joint innovation results in life science, materials science, and deep-space astronomy were also released at the same event under a collaborative program with partner universities and research institutions.

On AI safety, the laboratory articulates what it terms an "AI-45° balance principle," arguing that AI safety and capability should develop in rough equilibrium over the long run, and describes a causal-reasoning-based technical path toward trustworthy AGI through three progressive stages it labels broad alignment, interventionability, and reflective capacity. The site's held facts record no litigation or MCP server registrations associated with the organization.
